is_anopheles.evidence: The study uses Anopheles gambiae s.s. (Kisumu KDR strain).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper mentions the Kisumu KDR strain has L1014F and L1014S knockdown resistance alleles (page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper states the strain has these alleles but does not provide genotype counts (RR/RS/SS) or frequencies for the mosquitoes used in this specific study; it refers to previous studies for the characterization of the strain.

african_field_population.evidence: The mosquitoes used are from a laboratory colony (Kisumu KDR strain) maintained at the Ifakara Health Institute, not a field-collected population.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study evaluating the effect of chlorfenapyr-treated nets on P. falciparum infection in mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted in Bagamoyo, Tanzania.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was conducted between September 2021 and August 2022.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new experimental procedure.

supplement.evidence: The paper provides the necessary data for its own experimental results.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the effect of sub-lethal exposure to chlorfenapyr-treated nets on P. falciparum infection in a laboratory-reared pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.s. strain (Kisumu KDR). It found that exposure significantly reduced oocyst and sporozoite prevalence and oocyst intensity.
exclusion_reasons: The study uses a laboratory colony (Kisumu KDR) rather than a field-collected population.
The paper does not report new genotype data for the mosquitoes used in the experiments; it only references the known resistance status of the laboratory strain.
